title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets out two parallel lists of conjectural 'descriptions' (realizations) of motives. It is the planning sheet for the section 'Motifs et cristaux sur corps local' announced on p.3.

(A) Motives over a number field k (or over Q̄ for items 3 and 4). Each item is a linear-algebra or analytic category that the motives should embed into, at least conjecturally fully faithfully.
1) 'Double visage Betti–De Rham': a Q-vector space H_B (after choosing a complex embedding), a k-vector space H_dR with its Hodge filtration, and the comparison isomorphism H_B⊗C ≅ H_dR⊗_k C. This is a period structure.
2) 'Double visage Betti–Hodge': H_B together with a Hodge decomposition of H_B⊗C, i.e. a polarizable Q-Hodge structure plus the k-structure.
3) A pure Hodge structure alone, for k = Q̄. The deleted words 'Betti + bigrad.' show he means a Betti lattice plus a bigrading of H_B⊗C.
4) 'Betti – (Gauss-)Manin', for k = Q̄. Plausibly: spread the motive over a variety S of finite type over Q and record the Betti local system together with the algebraic Gauss–Manin connection, i.e. a Riemann–Hilbert/period type description.
5) 'Betti – Tate': H_B plus the Galois-equivariant comparison H_B⊗Q_l ≅ H_et.
6) 'De Rham filtré cristallin': H_dR with its Hodge filtration and, at the primes of good reduction, the crystalline Frobenius structure.

(B) p-divisible groups up to isogeny over a local field K. K is the fraction field of a complete DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic p. These groups are viewed as 'pseudo-motifs', i.e. the p-adic analogue of motives with only Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1. The Tate realization is written explicitly: a finite-dimensional Q_p-space N (the rational Tate module) with a bigrading on N⊗_{Q_p} C, C = Ĉ_K. This is the Hodge–Tate decomposition of Tate 1967.
The primed list mirrors (A):
- 3') a 'Hodge-p' (Hodge–Tate) structure, only up to finite extension of K. Hodge–Tate data alone are invariant only for an open subgroup or after finite extension, much as a bare Hodge structure forgets the field.
- 2') 'double visage Tate–Hodge': the Galois module together with its Hodge–Tate decomposition. This is the analogue of Betti–Hodge.
- 5') Tate: the Galois p-adic module V_p(G). By Tate's theorem this is fully faithful on p-divisible groups up to isogeny.
- 6') filtered crystal: a finite-dimensional vector space over the Witt fraction field K_0, with a σ-semilinear Frobenius, a filtration (Hodge) and a grading. This is essentially a filtered Dieudonné module, i.e. Fontaine's filtered φ-module.

The closing question 'Par quoi remplacer 1', 4' ??' asks what the p-adic analogues are of the Betti–De Rham comparison (1) and of Betti–Gauss–Manin (4). Item 1 would be a comparison isomorphism V_p ⊗ (?) ≅ D ⊗ (?) linking the Tate module and the crystal. That is exactly the 'mysterious functor' problem.

The next page attacks this group-theoretically. It compares the Tannakian groups G (Tate side) and G' (crystal side) via an isomorphism α over C, with splittings of extensions of the Galois group π by G(C). It uses the cyclotomic character χ: π→Q_p^*, an early torsor-of-periods style approach.
errors: 6') says the filtered crystal is a vector space 'sur K'. The Frobenius-semilinear structure lives over K_0 = Frac W(k), and the Hodge filtration lives on D⊗_{K_0} K. These coincide only when K is unramified. When e>1 the filtration cannot simply be put on the K_0-space; this is precisely the ramified difficulty treated later by Fontaine, Laffaille, Breuil and Kisin.

Hodge–Tate data (3') do not determine a p-divisible group up to isogeny: the functor is not fully faithful. Grothendieck seems aware of this ('mod ext. finie de K'), and the full description needs the Galois module (5') or the filtered crystal (6').

The essential image of 6' is not all filtered φ-modules but only the (weakly) admissible ones with Hodge–Tate weights in {0,1} (Fontaine; Colmez–Fontaine 2000; Breuil, Kisin). The page does not address the essential image.

ideas.what: A motive is described by a system of realizations (Betti, de Rham, Hodge, l-adic, crystalline) linked by comparison isomorphisms.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (oral), formalized by Deligne (1979, 1989), Jannsen (1990), Fontaine–Perrin-Riou
ideas.where_published: Discussed in Grothendieck's letters and talks; formalized in published form by others

ideas.what: Describing motives over Q̄ by the Betti local system plus the Gauss–Manin connection (item 4).
ideas.modern_name: Riemann–Hilbert/period description of motives via variations; Gauss–Manin systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda, Deligne; motivic aspects later André
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) for algebraic de Rham; not as a motivic realization

ideas.what: The rational Tate module of a p-divisible group, with a 'bigrading' on N⊗C (Hodge–Tate decomposition) viewed as a p-adic Hodge structure ('structure de Hodge-p').
Filtered Dieudonné crystal (σ-semilinear Frobenius on a K_0-space plus Hodge filtration) as a description of p-divisible groups up to isogeny.
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', ICM Nice 1970; 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné', Montréal 1974

ideas.what: The question of what replaces the Betti–De Rham comparison in the p-adic setting, i.e. a direct comparison between the Tate module and the filtered crystal.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor'; Fontaine's period rings B_cris, B_dR, B_st and the C_cris/C_dR comparison theorems
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 talk and Montréal lectures (the 'problème du foncteur mystérieux')

ideas.what: Viewing p-divisible groups over local fields as 'pseudo-motifs' with a full list of realizations parallel to motives over number fields.
ideas.modern_name: p-adic Hodge theory as the p-adic analogue of Hodge theory for motives

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks for a p-adic replacement of the Betti–Gauss–Manin description (4'), separately from the Betti–De Rham comparison (1'). The 1' question was answered by Fontaine's B_dR/B_cris. No canonical 'p-adic Gauss–Manin realization' of a single Galois representation was proposed at the time. Retrospectively, the natural candidates are Berger's theorem (de Rham representations ↔ p-adic differential equations with Frobenius structure on the Robba ring, 2002), Sen's operator, and Scholze's relative p-adic Hodge theory. The parallel 'Gauss–Manin ↔ (φ,Γ)/differential equation' as a fourth p-adic realization is not usually phrased as answering a Grothendieck question.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows the mysterious-functor problem was conceived as part of a systematic dictionary that also included a differential-equation (Gauss–Manin) realization. That anticipates the role of p-adic differential equations in p-adic Hodge theory. This is a modest historiographical point, not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The core content is the mysterious-functor problem and the realization philosophy, both known and attributed to Grothendieck through the published ICM 1970 and Montréal texts. The added details are of modest interest: the explicit parallel list Betti/Hodge/Tate/crystal versus Tate/Hodge-Tate/crystal, the 'Hodge-p structure' terminology, and the separate question about a p-adic Gauss–Manin analogue.
transcription_corrections: The numbering in part (B) is overwritten in bold. 'double visage Tate – Hodge' appears to be numbered 2' (analogue of 2 Betti–Hodge), not 1', and 'structure de Hodge-p' is 3'. This is consistent with the closing question asking about the missing 1' and 4'.
'Tate (module galoisien l-adique)': in the context of p-divisible groups this should be read as p-adic. The handwriting is ambiguous, and Grothendieck may have written l by habit.
'Galois généré des pseudo-motifs' is uncertain. The sense is that p-divisible groups mod isogeny are viewed as (generating) 'pseudo-motifs'.
In the header 'corps de nbs [-?-] k', the crossed-out symbol before k is illegible; the intended reading is 'corps de nombres k'.
'à corps rés. p-parfait' should probably be read as 'à corps résiduel parfait (de car. p)'.
In 6' the bracket reads roughly '[vectoriel de dim finie sur K, un Witt σ-semi-linéaire, à filtration, graduation]', i.e. a Frobenius that is σ-semilinear over Witt vectors.
